note.text: Pipelines carry suitable fluids, such as oil or gas, along fixed links using appropriate pressure and control systems. They can support continuous bulk movement, but require substantial construction, maintenance and monitoring. They do not carry every kind of freight or replace passenger transport. Leakage and route impacts require assessment; fixed infrastructure also makes changing destinations costly.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to explain pipeline suitability and a related constraint. Builds on: specialised fixed-route transport. Leads to: global flows and telecommunications.

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: The Chad–Cameroon petroleum pipeline project connects oil-producing areas in Chad with an offshore loading facility near Kribi in Cameroon. This is a route example, not a current flow, tariff or operating claim. A fictional liquid-fuel route can illustrate fixed-link benefits while a furniture shipment illustrates a cargo that cannot use that system.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Ask whether the material is suitable for the system, whether origins and destinations fit the fixed route and how leakage would be detected and managed. Compare both operating advantages and construction or environmental constraints.

pick.q: A fictional oil route has stable endpoints and suitable fluid cargo. Why might a pipeline be considered?
pick.r: It can support bulk fluid movement along a fixed link
w: It carries every passenger directly home
It carries all furniture without transformation
It avoids every construction cost
e: It is not a passenger system.
Finished furniture is unsuitable for this liquid pipeline.
Construction requires capital and land works.
pick.y: Suitability depends on cargo and route conditions.

pick.q: A furniture seller wants to send assembled tables through an oil pipeline. What is the problem?
pick.r: The cargo is unsuitable for that system
w: The tables need only a telephone number
All transport modes accept every cargo
Pipelines are designed for doorstep furniture delivery
e: Contact information does not change cargo properties.
Systems have different cargo requirements.
A fixed fluid link does not serve tables.
pick.y: Match physical properties to the designed system.

pick.q: A pipeline proposal claims burial removes all environmental concerns. What is missing?
pick.r: Leakage, construction impacts and monitoring assessment
w: Proof that fluids cannot leak
An assumption no land is used
A claim maintenance is unnecessary
e: Fluids can escape if a system fails.
Routes occupy and disturb land during construction.
Maintenance remains necessary.
pick.y: Being underground does not eliminate impacts.
